### Subject: Opinion on includibility of FCCB conversion gain in book profit for MAT computation under Section 115JB

---

## 1. Purpose and Basis of this Opinion

This opinion is issued pursuant to our engagement letter dated [●], and is based solely on the facts and representations furnished by the management of Comet Pharma Limited, and on the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act, 1961, applicable rules, notifications, circulars, and judicial precedents as they stand on the date hereof. We have not independently verified the facts provided to us. This opinion is addressed solely to, and for the sole use of, Comet Pharma Limited for the specific purpose stated herein, and should not be relied upon, quoted, or disclosed to any third party without our prior written consent.

## 2. Statement of Facts

On conversion of its Foreign Currency Convertible Bonds into equity shares at a price below the carrying liability value, Comet Pharma Limited recorded a notional gain of INR 30 crore through its profit and loss account, as required under Ind AS 109.

## 3. Issue for Consideration

Whether the notional FCCB conversion gain credited to the profit and loss account must be included in 'book profit' for the purpose of Minimum Alternate Tax under Section 115JB.

## 4. Relevant Legal Framework

- Section 115JB
- Section 115JB(2A)-(2C)
- Explanation 1 to Section 115JB


## 5. Judicial Precedents Considered

- Apollo Tyres Ltd v. CIT, (2002) 255 ITR 273 (SC)
- CIT v. Bhari Information Tech. Sys. (P) Ltd (2011)

## 6. Analysis

Following Apollo Tyres, the Assessing Officer's power to alter book profits certified in accordance with the Companies Act is confined to the specific additions and deductions expressly permitted under Section 115JB; the FCCB conversion gain, although non-cash and notional, is not among the items specifically excludible under Explanation 1 and does not qualify as a capital receipt carved out from book profit.

## 7. Conclusion / Opinion

The FCCB conversion gain of INR 30 crore is includible in book profit for MAT computation under Section 115JB.

**Confidence level:** High
